observation.visible_scene: Extreme macro close-up of a single human eye, framed by reddish-brown skin, a dark eyebrow at the top, and dense upper/lower lashes. The iris is gray-blue and does not blink or move appreciably across the clip. Embedded in the pupil/iris is a reflected scene: a child in a mustard-yellow sweater stands near center in front of a bright radial glow; to the child's left is a pale, white-coated figure; to the right is faint reddish graffiti-like text on a wall. The reflection is the main animated element, while the eye anatomy itself stays essentially fixed.
visible_changes: Within the reflection, the white figure on the left gradually becomes more solid and defined: it starts as a faint vertical smear and resolves into a clearer white-coated form with two leg shapes at the bottom and a small bright point of light near its top.
The bright light point associated with the white figure intensifies and sharpens over the segment.

The child in the yellow sweater rotates within the reflection from a more frontal stance (head turned left) toward a left-facing profile oriented toward the white figure; this is a change of pose/orientation, not a translation across the frame.
The radial glow behind the child and the overall brightness of the reflected scene shift subtly, with the white figure's area brightening relative to the start.
The reddish graffiti on the right remains in roughly the same position, fading/softening slightly rather than moving.
The eye, lashes, eyebrow and iris pattern remain static; no blink or saccade is visible, so the apparent motion is confined to the reflected image, not to the eye.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the reflected scene physically depicts and whether the eye belongs to the child or to another observer.
The cause of the bright light and the white figure's appearance, and any action before or after this cropped window.
Whether the reflection's changes are a real optical reflection, an inserted image, or a memory/dream overlay.
uncertain_details: Any camera drift or slow zoom is minimal and not clearly distinguishable from the static framing; treat camera motion as uncertain.
Whether the child raises or extends an arm toward the white figure is ambiguous due to the small, soft reflection.
The exact identity and posture of the white-coated figure remain unclear throughout.

Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
